 Women and children play on a beach in Bandar Abbas, Iran, on Friday looking out on the Strait of Hormuz
 Credit : ISNA via AP/Amirhosein Khorgooi
 Our Foreign Staff
 Updated 
 15 November 2026 6:11pm GMT
 Published 
 15 November 2026 2:42pm GMT
 A supertanker carrying more than two million barrels of oil sank after it struck a mine in the Strait of Hormuz , Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC) said.
 The ship was one of two vessels that hit mines while transiting the vital trade corridor, the group claimed. There has been no independent confirmation of the incidents.
 Since the outbreak of the Iran war in late February, the Islamic Republic has heavily restricted traffic through the strategic waterway, insisting vessels use routes it has authorised.
 It has frequently targeted ships that transit without its authorisation.
 In response, the US imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports and helped tankers travel the strait, which carries about one-fifth of global oil annually in peacetime.
 The American military recently claimed to have cleared all mines from the main routes through the waterway.
 “Over the past few hours, two oil tankers travelling along an unauthorised route in the southern part of the Strait of Hormuz struck naval mines, resulting in massive explosions and fire,” the IRGC said in a statement carried by state television on Sunday.
 “One of these vessels – a super tanker carrying over two million barrels of crude oil – sank in the southern waters of the Persian Gulf,” it added.
 It did not specify the names or origins of the tankers.
 An image taken from an IRGC video purportedly showing a vessel that hit a mine in the Strait of Hormuz last week
 Credit : AFP via Getty Images/ IRIB NEWS AGENCY
 In recent weeks Tehran has made several announcements saying ships had caught fire in the strait, often claiming they struck mines.
 US Central Command (Centcom), which oversees American military operations in the region, has been supporting ships traversing the waterway and said last month that it had helped Gulf countries export 1.5 billion barrels of oil via Hormuz since the summer.
 A British maritime monitor on Sunday said it was aware of a report by Indian shipping authorities of an attack on a tanker in the Gulf, but it was unclear whether it had been the incident announced by the IRGC.
 The UK Maritime Trade Operations centre said the damage and environmental impact were unknown, but the crew were safe.
 Separately on Sunday morning, Iran claimed to have attacked a US military base in Bahrain, which has been heavily targeted during the war.
 Bahrain’s military said it intercepted several Iranian attacks , “preventing them from reaching their intended targets”. The foreign ministry said air defence systems shot down Iranian drones.
 Explosions could be heard at around 4am local time (1am GMT), an AFP journalist said, with residents reporting a second series of blasts at around 6am.
 The interior ministry, posting on X, called on “residents to remain calm, proceed to the nearest safe location, and follow news through official channels”.
 The IRGC said: “The US air defence radar system at the Al-Riffa helicopter base in Bahrain was targeted by six drones belonging to the IRGC Aerospace Force.
 “The Strait of Hormuz is closed, and any aggression by the American enemy will be met with an even harsher and more forceful response.”
 Motorists in Tehran drive past an anti-Trump banner earlier this month
 Credit : Anadolu via Getty Images)/Fatemeh Bahrami
 Bahrain is among the Gulf countries that have weathered thousands of Iranian drone and missile strikes since the war began on Feb 28.
 The tiny island nation “rejects turning its territory into an arena for settling scores and holds Iran fully responsible for these attacks and their consequences”, the foreign ministry statement said.
 On Friday, the IRGC said its forces targeted a US early-warning radar system in Bahrain – the first strike against a Gulf country since early September.
 Centcom said it had shot down two Iranian drones targeting the Gulf island, reporting no casualties or damage in the attack.
 Donald Trump, whose steep reverse in midterm elections was partly blamed on the Iran war, planned to discuss the conflict at a trilateral meeting with his Chinese and Russian counterparts this week, an official said on Friday.
 Months of diplomacy have failed to resolve the war, which began with surprise US-Israeli strikes that killed Iran’s supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.
